text:
Tom: quick one from design: we keep talking about evidence blobs for attestation but ops raised privacy/size concerns. propose we standardize on an evidence-minimization approach: only store/verifiable hashes + optional zk-summary for sensitive signals.
Mei: love that direction. customers (especially private installs) don't want attest payloads leaving site. hashes + short-labelled metastrings would reduce telemetry PII.
Juan: practical tradeoffs: hashed evidence is fine for audit but debugging needs more detail. can we make a tiered reveal model: hash by default, reveal raw evidence to authorized reviewers with a signed request and TTL?
Priya: we need an access-control pattern for reveal. suggest: evidence_blob encrypted under customer/operator key; controlplane keeps only H(evidence). reveal flow: authorized operator posts signed reveal request -> audit-recorded -> controlplane issues temporary decrypt token to requester. keep TTL short.
Tom: for hosted mode, we could support a zero-knowledge style summary: attest_proof_summary that proves "runtime_is_trusted" without exposing hardware counters. reduces risk for customers while keeping the broker confident. not full ZKP, more like predicate attestations (e.g., measured_boot_ok:true).
Mei: also compress evidence for telemetry: telemetry should receive evidence_hash, attestor_type, trust_level (OK/WEAK), and small diagnostic code if failure. no raw attest data.
Juan: latency impact? adding an extra reveal step for debugs is fine, but the common path must be cheap: compute hash, verify signature, issue grant. avoid uploading raw blobs during normal flow.
Priya: operator UX: add CLI "redwood evidence-reveal --grant <rid> --reason <ticket-123> --approvers a,b" which generates a signed request and stores reveal audit entry. controlplane returns ephemeral access URL that expires. log everything.
Tom: consider policy: certain policies (e.g., legal-region, export-control) should never allow evidence reveal outside customer boundary. mark these as reveal=forbidden in policy metadata.
Mei: compatibility note: dedicated customers may opt into reveal for debugging; private default = forbidden unless operator config explicitly allows. hosted default = forbidden unless customer signs DPA. document this in RFC.
Juan: implementation detail: evidence hashes must include canonical serialization (deterministic) and salt per tenant to avoid cross-tenant correlation. include serialization spec in RFC appendix.
Priya: telemetry example record: {policy_id, decision, evidence_hash, attestor_type, trust_level, release_cid}. no fields with PII. correlate with request_id for postmortem.
Tom: add test cases: verify reveal flow audit trail, ensure revoked reveal tokens cannot be used, test hash canonicalization across runtimes. include harness scenario that simulates a reveal request and operator approval.
Mei: ops checklist: if customer asks for evidence, request steps: 1) open ticket 2) collect approvers 3) run redwood evidence-reveal 4) inspect ephemeral URL 5) rotate any keys if evidence shows compromise.
Juan: sounds good. i'll draft the canonicalization and salt rules. Priya you can draft CLI UX and audit schema. Mei i'll update RFC privacy section. Tom i'll pull into RFC and schedule a quick follow-up.
